test_title: PYST 12: SSC MTS 2023 - English (Held On: 06 Sept, 2023 Shift 3)
subject: english
question:
Select the most appropriate meaning of the underlined idiom.

The judge wanted to hear __straight from the horse’s mouth__.

options.text: In close vicinity to the juror

solution:
The correct answer is: **Directly from the person involved**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The idiom **"straight from the horse's mouth"** means getting information directly from the person who has direct knowledge or experience of it. (सीधे स्रोत से प्राप्त जानकारी)

 
 
• **Example: **If you want to know about the new project, ask John. He got the details straight from the horse's mouth.
 
 
 
• **"Directly from the person involved"** means obtaining information from the person who is directly connected with the matter. (प्रत्यक्ष रूप से शामिल व्यक्ति से जानकारी प्राप्त करना)
 
 
• **Example: **The CEO's resignation was confirmed directly from the person involved during the press conference.
 
 

Therefore, the correct answer is: **Option 2**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

Here are the other options explained along with their Hindi meanings and example sentences:

 
• **Directly from the lawyer** (प्रत्यक्ष रूप से वकील से): Receiving information from the lawyer.

 
 
• **Example: **The details of the case were provided directly from the lawyer during the hearing.
 
 
 
• **In close vicinity to the juror** (जूरी सदस्य के निकट): Being near to the juror.
 
 
• **Example: **The witness was seated in close vicinity to the juror to ensure clear communication.
 
 
 
• **Having ears which never fail** (ऐसे कान जो कभी असफल नहीं होते): Having perfect hearing ability.
 
 
• **Example: **Grandma has ears which never fail; she can hear even the faintest sounds.
